[[Michelle Saram]] ''(daughter-in-law)'' | other_names = | occupation = [[Hotel manager|Hotelier]], [[businessperson|businessman]] | years_active = | known_for = Founder of [[Aman Resorts]] | notable_works = }} '''Adrian Willem Ban Kwie Lauw-Zecha''' (born 1933), better known as '''Adrian Zecha''', is an Indonesian hotelier and founder of several international hotel companies including Aman Resorts, Regent Hotels, GHM Hotels and Azerai Resorts.{{cite web |title=Adrian Zecha – Chairman and Founder |url=https://asiasociety.org/files/uploads/286files/Adrian%20Zecha%20bio.pdf |access-date=2026-02-10 |publisher=Asia Society}} He is best known for founding Aman Resorts and for his influence on the development of luxury resort design and branding worldwide.{{cite web |title=The Story of Aman Resorts |url=https://www.architecturaldigest.com/story/aman-resorts-30th-anniversary |access-date=2026-02-11 |publisher=Architectural Digest}} Zecha was also part-owner of the renowned London’s Dorchester Hotel, and Bangkok’s The Sukhothai Hotel through his investment company.{{cite web|last1=Yang|first1=Patsy|title=Luang Prabang's slow pace of life is blissful|url=http://www.shanghaidaily.com/feature/travel/Luang-Prabangs-slow-pace-of-life-is-blissful/shdaily.shtml|work=[[Shanghai Daily]]|date=9 May 2017 |access-date=7 June 2017}}{{Cite web|title=Founders & History|url=https://azerai.com/founder-and-history/|access-date=27 July 2021|website=Azerai|language=en-US}} == Career == Zecha began his career in hospitality in the 1960s and was involved in the early development of Regent International Hotels in partnership with Four Seasons Hotels. He later co-founded GHM (Global Hotel Management), a company that operated luxury properties in Asia and beyond. In 1988, Zecha founded Aman Resorts, opening the first property, Amanpuri, in Phuket, Thailand. The brand became known for its low-density, design-focused luxury hotels and played a significant role in shaping the high-end resort market in Asia and later globally. == Personal life and education == Zecha was born in 1933 in Sukabumi, in what was then the Dutch East Indies (now Indonesia). He attended school in Jakarta before going on to study at Phillips Academy and later at Oxford University, where he read English literature. ==Family background== Zecha was born in [[Sukabumi]], Indonesia into the [[Lauw-Sim-Zecha family]], part of the [[Cabang Atas]] or Chinese gentry of colonial Indonesia. His family is of [[Peranakan Chinese]] and [[Czech people|Bohemian]] roots. He is a great-grandson of the late nineteenth-century magnate and mandarin [[Lauw Tek Lok]], the first [[Kapitan Cina|''Luitenant der Chinezen'']] of [[Bekasi]] (a high-ranking post in the civil bureaucracy) by the latter's controversial interracial marriage to [[Louisa Zecha]], an [[Indo people|''Indo'']] plantation owner of [[Bohemia]]n descent.{{cite book|last1=Tan|first1=Mely G.|title=The Chinese of Sukabumi: A Study of Social and Cultural Accommodation|date=1963|publisher=Cornell University|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qy6MrgEACAAJ&q=mely+g+tan+chinese+of+sukabumi|access-date=9 October 2017|language=en}}{{cite news|title=Adrian Zecha (né en 1933) : ses hôtels hors de prix de la chaîne Aman ressemblent au paradis|url=http://www.capital.fr/economie-politique/adrian-zecha-ne-en-1933-ses-hotels-hors-de-prix-de-la-chaine-aman-ressemblent-au-paradis-1099633|access-date=2 September 2017|work=Capital.fr|date=28 January 2016|language=fr-FR}} On being widowed, Louisa Zecha went on to marry another Chinese magnate, [[Sim Keng Koen]], the first Kapitein der Chinezen of Sukabumi, where her great-grandson Adrian Lauw Zecha was born. Zecha's father, the plantation owner [[William Lauw-Zecha|Aristide William Lauw-Zecha]], was the first native-born Indonesian to graduate from any American university, [[University of Iowa|Iowa University]], in 1923.{{cite book|last1=Lombard|first1=Denys|title=Nusa Jawa: Batas-batas pembaratan|date=1996|publisher=Gramedia Pustaka Utama|isbn=9789796054527|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ENuMmZ1CaTcC&pg=PA273|access-date=9 October 2017|language=id}}{{cite web|title=International Alumni Profiles|url=https://students.tufts.edu/student-affairs/living-campus/group-six/international-center/about-us/international-alumni-profiles|website=students.tufts.edu|publisher=Tufts Student Services|access-date=9 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170924071057/https://students.tufts.edu/student-affairs/living-campus/group-six/international-center/about-us/international-alumni-profiles|archive-date=24 September 2017|url-status=dead}} The connection with America continued with Zecha and his four brothers, who were all educated in the [[United States]].Hilditch, Tom. "Paradise Regained." Asiaweek.com, 15 June 2001. Zecha is also a cousin of the Malaysian royal, [[Che Engku Chesterina]] (née Sim-Zecha). His brother, Austen Zecha, was the founder of TBWA-ISC Group, an agency that is credited with the award-winning “Malaysia Truly Asia” campaign for Tourism Malaysia in 1999. Another brother, Alwin Zecha, was the founder and executive chairman of the Pacific Leisure Group, a destination management company with offices in 38 countries worldwide, and also served as a board member and Chairman for numerous other organizations, including PATA.{{citation needed|date=November 2025}} ==Early life and career== Zecha attended [[Dickinson College]] in [[Pennsylvania]].{{cite web |last1=Smith |first1=Jack |title=Feature: Aman's Man |date=March 2008 |url=https://robbreport.com/travel/destinations/feature-amans-man-aspx-237939/ |publisher=Robb Report}} Following graduation, he briefly attended Johns Hopkins University to pursue a medical degree on his father’s wishes, but later dropped out and instead pursued a Master in Journalism from Columbia University. In 1956, when President [[Sukarno]] nationalised the country's private businesses, many members of the Lauw-Sim-Zecha family fled to [[Colony of Singapore|Singapore]], the Netherlands, and the United States. At the time the 23-year-old Zecha was in [[New York City|New York]], working at [[Time (magazine)|''Time'' magazine]]. Between 1956 and 1958, Zecha worked at the magazine's [[Tokyo]] office. He took up a residence in [[Azabu-Jūban]] and rented a villa in [[Aburatsubo]]. During his time in Japan, he developed an appreciation for [[Ryokan|ryokan-style hotels]].{{Cite web |date=2025-01-19 |title=アマン創業者のゼッカさん アジアの美と文化を守る旅 NIKKEI The STYLE 「My Story」 |trans-title=Adiran Zecha's journey to preserve Asia's beauty |url=https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXZQOUD3019G0Q4A231C2000000/ |access-date=2025-01-19 |website=[[The Nikkei]] |language=ja}} In 1961, Zecha launched ''Asia Magazine'', the first regional newspaper colour supplement in [[Asia]]. When the magazine faltered a year later, [[Rupert Murdoch]] was persuaded by Zecha to invest in the magazine (in what was his first Asian investment). The magazine was a part of [[English language|English]] speaking families until 1998. It was held above water for its last ten years by Giro Semba and Olav Mueller-Uri until it finally closed in 1998. In 1970, Zecha started a new travel and lifestyle magazine named ''Orientations'' based in [[British Hong Kong|Hong Kong]]. With the advent of in-flight magazines, Orientations dropped its travel content and progressed over the years to become a publication focused on the arts of [[East Asia]], [[Southeast Asia]], [[South Asia]] and [[Himalayas|the Himalayas]]. It is now the leading magazine in this field and its contributors are renowned scholars and researchers from around the world. ==Hotels== Zecha's first experience of the hotel business was when a friend asked him to help the Marriott Hotel chain broker land deals in Asia. This experience led to Zecha joining with Robert Burns and Georg Rafael in 1972 to found Regent International Hotels, which was one of Asia's first luxury hotel groups.Barden, Carol. [http://www.travelandleisure.com/articles/aman-america "Amanresorts' New Jackson Hole Hotel"], ''Travel + Leisure'', 27 May 2009. Retrieved 8 February 2016.Zuckerman, Laurence. [https://www.nytimes.com/1992/08/20/business/worldbusiness/20iht-burn.html "Checking Out of Regent Hotels:How Chairman Was Bumped"], ''The New York Times'', 20 August 1992. Retrieved 8 February 2016. The trio built 12 hotels before Zecha sold his 30% stake for $30 million in 1986. He then moved into real estate speculation, forming an investment fund that, among other deals, bought [[Bangkok]]'s Regent Hotel and [[London]]'s Dorchester Hotel before eventually selling them. While in [[Phuket Province|Phuket]] looking for a site upon which to build a holiday home, Zecha was walking along Pansea Beach when he came across a coconut plantation which occupied a prime location.Miller, S. "Be My Guest, Please." ''Condé Nast Traveller'', Dec. 2007, p. 125. Plans to build a home on a site soon developed into an idea to build a small boutique resort in partnership with longtime friend Anil Thadani. The two spent mainly their own money as no banks would lend for the project due to the small number of planned rooms, instead of the 500-room hotel they thought would be more practical. [[Amanpuri]] opened in January 1988 at a cost of US$4 million with only 40 rooms. Its success, followed by that of Amandari in [[Bali]], confirmed to Zecha the viability of a chain of minimalist boutique resorts in remote, natural settings. In 1992, Zecha sold a controlling interest in Silverlink, the holding company which owned Aman Resorts, to Clement Vaturi, an old friend whose family owned the Hoteliere Immobliere chain of French hotels. Zecha was left with only 45% of the share holdings.Kan, W. [https://web.archive.org/web/20070816082200/http://www.time.com/time/business/article/0,8599,103987,00.html "'My Resorts Are Not Otherworldly.'"] ''Time'', 21 March 2001. The arrangement was satisfactory to both parties until Vaturi's controlling interest effectively came under the control of [[Los Angeles]]-based Colony Capital, a real estate investment fund. A lawsuit between Vaturi and Colony Capital promised to drag on, putting Zecha's plans to expand the number of Aman resorts on hold. Dispirited, and by now owning only 45% of Silverlink's shares, he resigned from his position as CEO in 1998. By 2000, [[Colony Capital]] and Vaturi had settled their lawsuit, which led to Vaturi getting his Silverlink shares back. He soon sold his shares to Lee Hing Development, a Hong Kong property fund which was affiliated with Thadani's Schroder Capital Partners (a [[Singapore]]-based fund). With the controlling investors now sharing his vision, Zecha returned as chairman and CEO. In the intervening period Zecha founded Maha Resorts, which opened its Hacineda de San Antonio in [[Mexico]] in October 2000. In 2007, Zecha announced that he had reached an agreement with [[DLF Ltd]], [[India]]'s largest real estate company, to form a partnership to acquire a controlling interest in Aman Resorts for US$250 million. DLF Group sold the company in 2013 to a joint venture between Russian real estate investor [[Vladislav Doronin]] and American entrepreneur [[Omar Amanat]] for US$358 million. Controversy ensued when Doronin announced that Zecha was stepping down as CEO and that he would assume the position. A London High Court injunction against Doronin reinstated Zecha as CEO, alleging that Doronin did not have board approval to remove him.[https://www.wsj.com/articles/london-court-rules-doronin-must-step-down-as-amanresorts-ceo-1405356659 "London Court Rules Doronin Must Step Down as Amanresorts CEO"] ''The Wall Street Journal'', 14 July 2014. The ruling, however, was limited, as it returned Zecha to his role for only 17 days. Olivier Jolivet, a longtime Aman executive, was appointed to the role which he held until February 2017.[http://fortune.com/2014/09/04/aman-resorts-nasty-battle-for-luxury-hotel-chain/ The global battle for the ultimate luxury hotel chain][https://www.ft.com/content/2138c5c0-9b17-11e4-b651-00144feabdc0 An exclusive look inside Aman Resorts' Tokyo hotel]{{cite web|last1=Gostelow|first1=Mary|title=Hoteliers On The Move, February 2017|url=http://www.travelmarketreport.com/articles/Hoteliers-On-The-Move-February-2017|publisher=Travel Market Report|access-date=11 May 2017}} In addition to his history at Aman Resorts, Zecha also chairman and director of General Hotel Management Ltd (GHM), a developer and manager of luxury hotels and resorts.[http://www.ghmhotels.com/en/ghm/home#team Team page], GHM Hotels Zecha was also a partner with Georg Rafael in Rafael Hotels Limited, a company that was sold to Mandarin Oriental Group in May 2000. In February 2017, Zecha began the soft opening for the first hotel under his new [[Azerai]] hotel brand which aims to provide more affordable lodging for adventurers and "the younger crowd".{{cite news|last1=Weinstein|first1=Jeff|title=HOTELS Profile: Adrian Zecha takes luxury downscale|url=http://www.hotelsmag.com/Industry/News/Details/72455?allowguest=true|access-date=7 June 2017|work=[[Hotels (magazine)|Hotels]]|date=31 March 2017|archive-date=5 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181105160717/http://www.hotelsmag.com/Industry/News/Details/72455?allowguest=true|url-status=dead}} This was followed in 2020 by a venture with Naru Developments to launch Azumi, a ryokan-inspired hotel brand based in Japan.{{Cite web |title=New Hospitality Brand Azumi To Launch In Japan |url=https://www.hospitalitynet.org/news/4101213.html |access-date=2022-08-27 |website=Hospitality Net |language=en-us}} ==Awards== In 2005 Adrian Zecha was awarded the Innovation Award at the 16th annual Hotel Investment Conference Asia Pacific (HICAP).[http://www.hotel-online.com/News/PR2005_2nd/Jun05_BobBurns.html "Robert Burns, Georg Rafael and Adrian Zecha to be Honored at the Upcoming 16th Annual Hotel Investment Conference Asia Pacific"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231006172256/https://www.hotel-online.com/News/PR2005_2nd/Jun05_BobBurns.html |date=6 October 2023 }}. Press release, hotel-online.com, 14 June 2006. In 2010 Adrian Zecha was awarded the 2010 Travel & Leisure Design Champion Award. The celebration was held at the [[California Academy of Sciences]] in [[San Francisco]].{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20140721133520/http://sfluxe.net/travel-leisure-design-awards/ "Travel And Leisure Design Awards"]}}, ''SFLUXE''. Retrieved 7 June 2016. In 2011, he was awarded an award for lifetime achievement during the International Luxury Travel Market event in [[Shanghai]].[http://www.luxurytravelmagazine.com/news-articles/amanresorts-adrian-zecha-receives-lifetime-achievement-award-16046.php "Amanresorts' Adrian Zecha receives Lifetime Achievement Award"], ''Luxury Travel Magazine''. Retrieved 8 February 2016. In 2018, he received the International Hotel Investment Forum (IHIF) Lifetime Achievement Award.{{Cite web |last=Thomas |first=Ben |date=2018-01-11 |title=Adrian Zecha to receive IHIF Lifetime Achievement Award |url=https://www.sleepermagazine.com/stories/people/adrian-zecha-to-receive-ihif-lifetime-achievement-award/ |access-date=2024-08-23 |website=Sleeper |language=en-US}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Zecha, Adrian}} [[Category:1933 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Hoteliers]] [[Category:Lauw-Sim-Zecha family]] [[Category:Cabang Atas]] [[Category:Indonesian people of Chinese descent]] [[Category:20th-century Indonesian businesspeople]] [[Category:20th-century Singaporean businesspeople]] [[Category:21st-century Indonesian businesspeople]] [[Category:21st-century Singaporean businesspeople]] [[Category:Indo people]]
